outcomes: A pull request opened from a fork gets the evidence upload, the putnami/observe commit status and the summary note, as a pull request from a branch does

The fork's run keeps its evidence document as an artifact, and a workflow_run job of the base repository relays it with the base repository's ID token and GITHUB_TOKEN, without running any code of the fork
A document that names another repository or another pull request is refused with a diagnostic, and the job still passes
nonGoals: Trusting the fork's analyses: the fork ran its own tests, so the report and the note show what the fork's run claims, under the run's page
GitLab: a merge request from a fork runs its pipeline in the target project when the project allows it, with the target's variables
Downloading the artifact in putnami observe: the workflow, or the action, downloads it

text: putnami observe --from-evidence <file> reads a change evidence document another run kept, instead of observing the checkout: it runs no Git command and reads no report.
It refuses a document over 64 MiB, or that does not validate against protocol/evidence v1, with the warning observe.evidence_refused.
--upload and --publish upload and publish it as for a run that observed the change.
Any observation flag, --evidence or --open with --from-evidence is a usage error, exit 2.

--from-evidence relays only in a GitHub Actions job a workflow_run event started for a pull_request run, with GITHUB_TOKEN to read the pull request and the commits; in any other job it gives the warning observe.evidence_refused and uploads and publishes nothing.
The repository, its numeric id and its host come from the job: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_REPOSITORY_ID and GITHUB_SERVER_URL.
The run, its attempt, its page, its head commit and its head repository come from workflow_run in the event payload.

The pull request is the one of the job's repository that workflow_run.pull_requests names at the run's head commit. For a fork it names none: observe asks the GitHub API, with GITHUB_TOKEN, for the open pull requests of the job's repository at the run's head owner and branch, and keeps the one at that commit.
The status goes on that commit and the note on that pull request.
Without one, a fork's run is refused; a run of the job's repository gives observe.pull_request_unresolved and publishes nothing.

The fork's document is untrusted: observe refuses, with observe.evidence_refused, one naming another provider, host, repository, repository id, CI or pull request than the job's, a commit other than the run's head or the pull request's merge commit, or a base other than that commit's first parent or an ancestor of the head, per the GitHub API. Nothing is uploaded or published, exit 0.
The relayed document takes its repository, pull request and run from the job, and names no branch of a fork.
Every text of the document reaches the summary note as a Markdown code span on one line, or as a count or an enumerated value the protocol checks, so it renders no link, mention, image or HTML.
The job log prints the counts and observe's own diagnostics, never a text of the document, so a line of the document cannot run a workflow command.
